title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing that believers should hear and follow Christ alone, not the law or prophets. He contrasts Moses (law) and Elijah (justice) with Jesus (love), urging the audience to focus on Christ for salvation and healing. Branham also discusses the role of the Holy Spirit as a tutor and the need for Christians to be salty examples.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham speaks on God's covenant with Abraham, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's seed and heirs to all promises. He encourages faith in God's Word despite symptoms, using the example of Abraham's unwavering belief. The sermon concludes with a call to separate from unbelief and trust in Jehovah-jireh, the Lord who provides.

title: What Does It Take To Make A Christian Life?
summary: William Branham discusses the necessity of the Holy Spirit in the church, contrasting the flexibility of new believers with the rigidity of old denominations. He uses the metaphor of new wine in new bottles to illustrate that God's Spirit cannot be contained by intellectualism or tradition. Branham emphasizes that true Christian life comes from the Holy Spirit controlling the believer, not from outward emotions or denominational affiliation.

title: The Infallible Proof of the Resurrection
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the foundational proof of Christianity. He contrasts the living Christ with dead religious founders, emphasizing that the resurrection is demonstrated through the Holy Spirit's work in believers today. He challenges the church to prove the resurrection by manifesting the same works Jesus did.

title: God Keeps His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the infallibility of God's Word, using the example of Isaiah's prophecy that the people could not believe in Jesus because the prophet had spoken it. He contrasts true faith in God's Word with empty religious formalism and warns against associating with those who deny the Bible's authority.

title: The Impersonation of Christianity
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for a genuine heart transformation by the Holy Spirit, contrasting it with intellectualism and emotional fanaticism. He emphasizes that true Christianity is not about outward acts or intellectual knowledge but about receiving a new heart and God's Spirit, which produces authentic fruit and order.

title: God Keeps His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the infallibility of God's Word, warning against false teachings and the spirit of the age. He uses the story of Ahab and Jehoshaphat to illustrate the danger of mixing truth with error, and calls believers to stand on the Word alone.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing that believers should hear Christ alone rather than the law or prophets. He contrasts the love of God with human religiosity and calls the church to rise above division and unbelief through faith in the Holy Spirit.

title: India Trip Report
summary: William Branham shares a report on his trip to India, emphasizing the need for the church to demonstrate the supernatural power of the Gospel as evidence of Christ's resurrection. He recounts a conversation with a Muslim who challenged Christians to produce the signs promised in Mark 16, and reflects on the poverty he witnessed in India, calling for unity and action among believers.

title: The Impersonation of Christianity
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for genuine Christianity, emphasizing that it is an experience of the Holy Spirit, not a denomination or intellectual creed. He uses Ezekiel 36:27 to discuss God's promise to put His Spirit in believers, and warns against impersonating Christianity through empty religious forms.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith that persists despite opposition. He draws parallels between Bartimaeus's faith in Jesus as the Son of David and the need for modern believers to trust in Christ for salvation and healing. The sermon includes an altar call for those who want Jesus to stand for them on judgment day.

title: SIRS, WE WOULD SEE JESUS
summary: William Branham speaks on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the importance of faith, the baptism of the Holy Spirit, and the power of God to heal, challenging the audience to experience the living Christ through His Word and Spirit.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith that stops Jesus despite distractions. He calls for reverence and faith, then prays for the sick, demonstrating the gift of discernment as a sign of Christ's presence.

title: And Then Jesus Came
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of Jesus' presence in the darkest moments, using the raising of Lazarus as a central text. He contrasts human weakness with divine power, emphasizing that Jesus is more than a prophet—He is God manifested in the flesh. Branham calls believers to stand firm on God's promises, as Jesus always arrives in the darkest hour.

title: Why Is It That So Many Christians Find It So Hard to Live the Christian Life?
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for a new heart and spirit, emphasizing that the Christian life is not about intellectualism or outward signs but about the indwelling Holy Spirit as the mainspring of the believer's life. He uses the analogy of an eagle and a watch to illustrate the freedom and power of a Spirit-filled life.

title: What Think Ye Of Christ?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question Jesus asked the Pharisees: 'What think ye of Christ?' He emphasizes that one's answer determines eternal destiny, healing, and salvation. Branham calls witnesses from Scripture and history to testify that Jesus is the virgin-born Son of God, and urges listeners to accept Him personally.

title: Divine Love
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of divine love, illustrating how God's love, when projected through believers, produces sovereign grace and miracles. He shares personal stories of love overcoming fear, including encounters with a violent man, hornets, a killer bull, and a dying opossum, to demonstrate that love casts out fear and brings healing.

title: God Keeps His Word 1
summary: William Branham preaches on God's faithfulness to His Word, using the story of Caleb and Joshua to contrast faith in God's promises with fear of circumstances. He warns against false signs and sensations, urging believers to stay grounded in Scripture.

title: God Keeps His Word 2
summary: William Branham preaches on the infallibility of God's Word, using the story of Micaiah and the false prophets to contrast true prophecy based on Scripture with deceptive signs and sensations. He warns against basing salvation on experiences, fasting, or prayer, emphasizing that only faith through the Word saves. Branham calls the church to return to the Bible and avoid being led astray by emotionalism and false doctrines.

title: The Good Shepherd Of The Sheep
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus as the Good Shepherd, using the metaphor of sheep to illustrate the relationship between believers and Christ. He emphasizes the shepherd's care, the sheep's dependence on the shepherd's voice, and the security of those who follow Him.

title: I Will Restore
summary: William Branham speaks at a Christian Businessmen's breakfast in Phoenix, using Joel 1:4 and 2:25 to discuss four destroyers (palmerworm, locust, cankerworm, caterpillar) that have eaten away at the church's heritage. He calls for a restoration of brotherly love, unity, and true worship, urging believers to overcome denominational divisions.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the redemptive name Jehovah-Jireh, using Abraham's willingness to sacrifice Isaac as a type of God providing the sacrifice. He emphasizes taking God at His Word unconditionally, as Abraham did, and applies this to divine healing and faith for the impossible.
themes: Christ as the fulfillment of Old Testament types

title: Washing Jesus' Feet
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of the Pharisee who invited Jesus to dinner but neglected to wash His feet, anoint His head, or give Him a kiss. He contrasts the cold, formal religion of the Pharisees with the heartfelt devotion of the sinful woman who washed Jesus' feet with her tears and anointed them with ointment. Branham calls for genuine love and worship of Jesus, warning against hypocrisy and worldliness.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham calls for unity among denominations, urging believers to focus on Christ rather than doctrinal differences. He contrasts the law, justice, and love, emphasizing that salvation comes only through hearing and obeying Jesus, the beloved Son of God.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Transfiguration, emphasizing that God's voice declared 'Hear ye Him'—pointing to Christ as the ultimate revelation of God's love, surpassing the law (Moses) and justice (Elijah). He calls the church to return to genuine love, holiness, and obedience to the Holy Spirit's tutoring through the Word, warning against worldliness and denominational barriers.

title: God In His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on four ways to see God: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. He uses nature, Scripture, and personal testimony to demonstrate God's presence and faithfulness, encouraging believers to have faith in God's promises and to recognize God dwelling within them.

title: Why Some People Can't Keep The Victory
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for a genuine Holy Spirit revival, using the analogy of the eagle to describe prophets and the new wine in new bottles to illustrate the necessity of flexible hearts to receive God's Spirit. He emphasizes that victory is kept not by intellectualism or denominationalism but by a new heart and spirit from God.
themes: The church as a living organism

title: The Lamb and the Dove
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of the Lamb and the Dove as representations of Christ and the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that true Christianity is not about outward demonstrations but about bearing the fruit of the Spirit through a changed nature. He calls for a return to holiness and surrender to the leading of the Holy Spirit.

title: Jehovah-jireh
summary: William Branham speaks on the redemptive name Jehovah-jireh, emphasizing God's unconditional covenant with Abraham and the importance of faith in God's promises. He encourages believers to separate from the world and trust in God's provision, using Abraham's example of unwavering faith.
themes: The Holy Spirit as the covenant seal

title: Then Jesus Came
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme that Jesus arrives in the darkest hour, using the story of Lazarus and other biblical examples to illustrate how Christ's presence brings hope and healing when all seems lost. He emphasizes that despite the world's troubles, Jesus is still the same yesterday, today, and forever, and He comes to those who trust in Him.

title: Corinthians, Book of Correction
summary: William Branham warns against basing salvation on sensations, gifts, or religious rituals, using 1 Corinthians 10 as a text. He emphasizes that true salvation comes only through a genuine new birth and love for God, not through outward experiences. He also condemns false prophets and worldly influences in the church.

title: The Second Coming of the Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the imminent Second Coming of Christ, urging the church to examine its spiritual condition and return to genuine devotion. He interprets current events as signs of the end times and calls for repentance and holiness.

title: The Communion
summary: William Branham preaches on the meaning of Communion as a commemoration of Christ's finished work, not a means of salvation. He draws parallels between the Old Testament Passover and the Lord's Supper, emphasizing the importance of testing and faithfulness. The sermon includes a personal testimony of his own Gethsemane experience and an altar call.

title: The Perfection
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of perfection, explaining that the law could not make worshippers perfect, but Christ's one sacrifice perfects forever those who are sanctified. He emphasizes that salvation is not by works but by grace through faith in Christ's atoning blood.

title: The Entombment
summary: William Branham preaches on the infallibility of God's Word, using the examples of Job, Abraham, and other Old Testament saints who trusted God's promises. He describes Jesus' descent into hell and paradise during His entombment, His victory over Satan, and the assurance of resurrection for those in Christ.

title: The Great And Mighty Conqueror
subtitle: 57-0421S
summary: William Branham delivers an Easter sermon comparing earthly conquerors like Napoleon and Hitler to the ultimate Conqueror, Jesus Christ, who conquered sin, death, and hell through His resurrection. He emphasizes that Christ's victory is complete and believers can rejoice in the finished work of salvation.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He calls for spiritual healing and unity among believers, and prepares the congregation for a healing service where the Holy Spirit will manifest the works of Jesus.

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on Matthew 12:42, comparing the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom with the generation that rejected Jesus. He emphasizes that God vindicates His gifts, and people are obligated to believe when the sign is proven. Branham contrasts the queen's faith and sacrifice with the unbelief of his own generation, warning of judgment.

title: Stand Still
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for believers to stand still and trust God's promises amidst a flustered world. Using the biblical account of Caleb and Joshua, he contrasts faith in God's Word with fear of circumstances, urging the church to remain calm and focused on Christ. He emphasizes that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that faith can bring Him to a standstill to answer prayer.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing that God's voice from the cloud commanded 'Hear ye Him,' signifying that the law and prophets are fulfilled in Christ. He urges believers to listen to the Holy Spirit as their teacher and to set aside denominational divisions.

title: Love
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of love as the most powerful force, because God is love. He illustrates through personal stories how love changes atmospheres and brings about miracles, including healing and protection.

title: Life
summary: William Branham preaches on the true meaning of life, contrasting worldly pleasures with the eternal life found in God. He emphasizes that only through knowing Christ and being born again can one experience true life, and warns against perversions that lead to death.

title: God Keeps His Word
subtitle: 57-0613A
summary: William Branham preaches on God's faithfulness to His Word, using the story of Caleb and Joshua from Numbers 13. He contrasts their faith with the unbelief of the other spies, urging believers to stand on God's promises despite obstacles. The sermon calls for a return to biblical foundations and personal consecration.
themes: unity in the Body of Christ

title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham preaches on the soul's thirst for God, contrasting the perverted life of sin with the eternal life found in Christ. He uses the imagery of a deer panting for water to illustrate the desperate need for the Holy Spirit, and calls believers to drink from the inexhaustible fountain of Christ.

title: The Queen of the South
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing a parallel to the need for seeking Christ and the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that God confirms His Word through supernatural works, and calls for sincere faith and repentance.
themes: The Holy Spirit as a gift

title: Believe from the Heart
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of believing from the heart rather than the intellect, using the example of a bridge builder who tested every material before building. He emphasizes that God tests every believer and places them in the Church as witnesses, and that true faith comes from a heart anchored in God's Word.

title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham preaches on the soul's thirst for God, contrasting worldly pleasures with true spiritual life. He warns against quenching that holy thirst with sin, church membership without conversion, or religious activity without genuine surrender. Using Psalm 63 and the metaphor of a deer fleeing wild dogs, he calls for a deep, desperate longing for God alone.
themes: the danger of quenching the Spirit

title: The Eagle In Her Nest
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of an eagle stirring her nest to describe how God challenges and lifts His Church. He contrasts the eagle's heavenly nature with earthbound chickens, urging believers to set their faith on God's promises and soar above worldly cares. The sermon includes testimonies of healings and deliverances, and calls for a fresh move of the Holy Spirit.
themes: Eagle as type of the Church
The Holy Spirit as Mother Eagle

title: As the Eagle Stirreth Up Her Nest
summary: William Branham uses the eagle as a metaphor for the Church, describing how God feeds His people through His Word, lifts them to heavenly places, and stirs the nest to prepare them for spiritual flight. He contrasts the eagle's high ambitions and dependence on God with the earthbound nature of worldly religion, urging believers to hold fast to God's promises.

title: He Was To Pass That Way
summary: William Branham uses the story of Zacchaeus to illustrate how God works through prayer and humility to bring people to Jesus. He encourages believers to be determined to see Jesus, regardless of social status or reputation, and emphasizes that Jesus knows each person's heart and calls them by name.

title: The Great Commission
summary: William Branham speaks on the Great Commission from Mark 16, emphasizing that signs and wonders should follow believers. He shares testimonies of his worldwide ministry, including a massive crusade in South Africa, and calls the church to return to the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He challenges the audience to see Jesus through the same works He performed in the Bible, such as healing the sick and knowing hearts, and calls for faith to experience His presence today.

title: God Manifesting His Gifts
summary: William Branham preaches on God's pattern of sending gifts and witnesses throughout history, using the Queen of Sheba's journey to see Solomon's wisdom as a type of seeking God's gifts. He warns against rejecting the Holy Spirit's work and calls for faith in the resurrected Christ who manifests His presence through spiritual gifts.
themes: God's witnesses rejected by religious systems
The Queen of Sheba as a model of seeking
The sign of Jonah as perpetual witness
The Holy Spirit's work in gifts
Divine healing as a sign of Christ's resurrection

title: God Projecting His Love
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of God's love, using John 3:16 as the central text. He contrasts human love (phileo) with divine love (agapao), sharing personal testimonies of how love overcame fear and produced miracles, including healing the sick and taming wild animals. He emphasizes that love is the greatest force and that God's love, when received as a pardon, brings salvation and healing.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Transfiguration, emphasizing that God commands us to hear His Son Jesus rather than the law or prophets. He calls for genuine Christian love and obedience over denominationalism and worldly distractions.

title: The Mighty Conqueror
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus Christ as the ultimate conqueror who overcame sin, death, hell, and the grave. He contrasts worldly conquerors like Napoleon with Christ's victory at Calvary and resurrection, urging believers to have faith and be gallant in their Christian walk.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith in Jesus as the Lamb of God who heals and saves. He encourages the congregation to accept Christ and trust in His power for physical and spiritual healing.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the compound redemptive name Jehovah-Jireh, emphasizing that God provides a sacrifice and that all redemptive names of God are inseparable. He uses the story of Abraham to illustrate unconditional covenant and faith, and shares a testimony about a photograph of the Angel of the Lord taken in Houston.

title: The Greatest Gift In The Bible
summary: William Branham preaches on the greatest gift in the Bible: Eternal Life, which is found only through knowing Jesus Christ. He contrasts true life with perverted life, using nature illustrations and personal stories to emphasize the soul's thirst for God.

title: Time-Tested Memorials of God
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of memorials, contrasting earthly monuments that decay with God's eternal Word. He uses biblical examples like Joshua's stones, Lot's wife, and the testing of a bridge builder to illustrate that true memorials are built on faith and God's unchanging promises.

title: Hebrews, Chapter One
summary: William Branham begins a verse-by-verse study of the Book of Hebrews, emphasizing the supremacy of Christ over prophets and angels. He discusses the importance of grounding experience in Scripture, using the Urim and Thummim as a type of God's Word. Branham also contrasts the law and grace, and explains the Trinity as one God in three offices.

title: Hebrews, Chapter Two #1
subtitle: 57-0825M
summary: William Branham preaches on Hebrews chapter 2, emphasizing the importance of giving earnest heed to the Word of God and not letting it slip. He contrasts the steadfastness of the word spoken by angels (prophets) with the greater salvation spoken by the Lord Jesus, confirmed by signs and wonders. Branham warns against neglecting this great salvation and calls for unity among believers.
themes: Confirmation of the Word by signs

title: Hebrews, Chapter Two
summary: Paul continues his exposition of Hebrews chapter 2, emphasizing the importance of not neglecting the great salvation brought by Christ. He contrasts the ministry of angels (prophets) with the superior ministry of Jesus, who was made lower than angels to taste death for every man. Branham exhorts believers to give earnest heed to the Word, to place God first, and to recognize the signs of the times through the Holy Spirit's work.

title: Hebrews, Chapter Two #3
summary: William Branham continues his teaching on Hebrews chapter 2, emphasizing the importance of not neglecting so great a salvation. He discusses Paul's conversion and his three years of study in Arabia, the nature of Christ as the Logos and High Priest, and how God became man to suffer and sympathize with humanity, ultimately conquering death.

title: Hebrews, Chapter Three
summary: William Branham teaches from Hebrews chapter 3, emphasizing that experiences must be validated by Scripture. He shares testimonies of healings and discusses the importance of comparing Scripture with Scripture, warning against neglecting the great salvation offered through Christ.

title: Hebrews, Chapter Four
summary: William Branham continues his teaching on the Book of Hebrews, focusing on the fourth chapter. He discusses the concept of God's rest, contrasting the Sabbath day with the true rest found in Christ. Branham emphasizes that unbelief prevented the Israelites from entering God's rest, and warns believers not to harden their hearts but to mix the Word with faith.

title: Hebrews, Chapter Five and Six
summary: William Branham continues his study of the Book of Hebrews, focusing on the call to go on to perfection beyond the foundational doctrines of Christ. He emphasizes that true perfection comes only through Christ, not through religious works or experiences, and discusses the eternal redemption secured by Christ's blood.
themes: The Word of God as standard

title: Hebrews, Chapter Six 2
summary: William Branham continues his study of Hebrews chapter 6, emphasizing the need to move beyond foundational doctrines like baptism and laying on of hands toward perfection in Christ. He discusses eternal security, election, and the impossibility of true believers falling away, using the analogy of rain falling on both wheat and cockleburs to illustrate that outward religious experiences do not guarantee salvation.

title: Hebrews, Chapter Six 3
summary: William Branham continues his study of Hebrews, focusing on the 7th chapter and the theme of faith anchored in God's unchangeable Word. He emphasizes the new birth, the security of the believer, and the hope that serves as an anchor of the soul within the veil.

title: Hebrews, Chapter Seven
summary: William Branham teaches on Hebrews chapter 7, focusing on the mysterious figure of Melchisedec, whom he identifies as God Himself—without father, mother, beginning or end. He draws parallels between Abraham's rescue of Lot and Christ's redemption of fallen humanity, and emphasizes the importance of separation from the world, church discipline, and the principle of fighting for souls rather than money.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that the same works Jesus did—healing, discerning thoughts, and revealing the Father—are still performed today through the Holy Spirit. He calls the congregation to personal faith, not in man or gifts, but in the Giver, God, and demonstrates the gift of discernment by revealing specific conditions and needs of individuals in the audience.
themes: the last sign before Christ's return

title: Hebrews, Chapter Seven 2
summary: William Branham discusses the sovereignty of the local church, the nature of Melchisedec as an eternal priest, and the distinction between law and grace. He emphasizes that true holiness comes from Christ, not human effort, and warns against willful unbelief.

title: Questions and Answers Hebrews Part I
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including everlasting punishment, the children of the kingdom being cast into outer darkness, the extent of Christ's atonement, and water baptism. He emphasizes the distinction between everlasting (limited time) and eternal (no beginning or end), explains the sealing of the 144,000 Jews as temple eunuchs, and defends the doctrine of election and the use of Jesus' Name in baptism.
themes: the sealing of the Holy Spirit

title: Questions and Answers Hebrews Part II
summary: William Branham opens with personal updates about his wife's recovery and upcoming travel to visit F.F. Bosworth. He then addresses various church matters, including funerals and a controversial medical case. The main teaching covers the distinction between the new birth and the Baptism of the Holy Spirit, and the location of Jesus' spirit during the three days in the tomb.
themes: Baptism of the Holy Spirit vs. New Birth
Witness of Christ in Death and Hades

title: Questions and Answers Hebrews Part III
summary: William Branham answers Bible questions about Cain's wife, the spirits in prison from 1 Peter 3:19, and the stones in Revelation 21:19-20. He explains that Cain married his sister, that the 'angels' who sinned were human messengers, and that the twelve foundation stones represent the twelve tribes of Israel.

title: I Stand At The Door And Knock
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:14-20, focusing on Jesus standing at the door and knocking. He emphasizes that Christ seeks entrance into every compartment of the believer's heart, including doors of selfishness, pride, and faith. Branham urges listeners to open their hearts fully to Jesus as Lord.
themes: Jesus knocking at the heart's door

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the signs of the times, the need for faith, and the manifestation of God's power through the Church, drawing parallels between Jesus' ministry and the present day.

title: The Door Of The Door
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3, focusing on the Laodicean church age and the lukewarm condition of the modern church. He urges believers to open every compartment of their hearts to Christ, not just as Savior but as Lord, and to have faith in His promises for healing and spiritual renewal.

title: And Then Jesus Came
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of Jesus' presence in the darkest moments, using the story of Lazarus to illustrate that Jesus comes when hope seems lost. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His works continue through the Church by the Holy Spirit.
themes: The Holy Spirit's work in the Church

title: Speak to This Mountain
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of faith and the spoken word, using the account of Jesus cursing the fig tree as a text. He emphasizes that faith is the substance of things hoped for and that believers can speak to their mountains (problems) and believe they are already moved. He shares testimonies of miracles, including a fish raised from the dead, to illustrate God's simplicity and power.

title: The Great Shining Light
summary: William Branham preaches on the Christmas story, focusing on the wise men and the star that led them to Jesus. He draws parallels between the star's guidance and the Holy Spirit's leading today, urging believers to reflect Christ's light in a dark world.

title: Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of personal experience with God to develop faith, using biblical examples like David, Moses, and the woman at the well. He emphasizes that faith comes through experience and that God confirms His Word through signs and wonders today.
